edition.intro: This week's edit is all about smart outerwear, shoes that finish an outfit, and easy ways to refresh what you already own.

items.title: The 5 Types of Coats Every Guy Should Own
items.snippet: A great winter outfit starts with the right outerwear.
items.headline: The Five Coats Worth Knowing, Starting With the Topcoat and Raglan
items.summary: Esquire argues that your coat is the most visible and hardworking part of a winter wardrobe, so it deserves real thought. The excerpt walks through the polished wool topcoat, which works best in classic colors and a length at or below the knee. It also covers the relaxed raglan overcoat, which has roomy shoulders that layer easily over chunky knits.
items.tip: Try on a coat over your thickest sweater before buying, so you know it will fit through the whole season.

items.title: Instead of Trainers, Stylish Over-50s Are Pairing Midi-Skirts With This Chic Winter Shoe
items.headline: Midi Skirts Meet Suede Boots, the Over-50 Favorite
items.summary: Who What Wear points to Uma Thurman's outfit of a satin midi skirt, a cream turtleneck and brown suede boots. Boots that reach calf height close the awkward gap trainers can leave under a flowing hem. The soft suede also adds a nice texture contrast with shiny fabric.
items.tip: Pair a midi skirt with a calf-height suede or leather boot and check that no gap shows between hem and shoe.

items.title: Not Jeans and Sambas—Fashion People Are Wearing This Trouser and Trainers Combination Instead
items.headline: Swap Jeans and Sambas for Grey Trousers and Chunky Trainers
items.summary: With the Samba craze fading, Who What Wear says the fresh move is a relaxed grey trouser worn with a chunkier trainer. Zoë Kravitz showed the idea with a beige trench and burgundy scarf, keeping it casual and easy. The soft grey feels new but still plays well with basic wardrobe staples.
items.tip: Wear your loosest grey or neutral trousers with your most comfortable trainers and a coat you already love.

items.title: 14 Best Barn Coats for Men in 2026, According to GQ Editors
items.snippet: The once-humble, still-hardy barn jacket looks just as killer on Auralee fiends as it does on the farm.
items.headline: Why the Barn Coat Is Worth a Look
items.summary: GQ describes the barn coat as a tougher, warmer relative of the chore jacket, originally made for outdoor work and now popular in cities. Its picks run from heritage classics to high-end designer versions. The key advice is to choose one with enough room to fit a sweater underneath and sturdy enough to last for years.
items.tip: Check that any jacket you consider has room for a sweater underneath before you commit.

items.title: Cecilie Bahnsen Rethinks the Fleece for Her Second Uniqlo Collaboration
items.snippet: The collection is a Scandi winter balletcore dream.
items.headline: Cecilie Bahnsen Gives the Uniqlo Fleece a Romantic Twist
items.summary: Designer Cecilie Bahnsen has made a second Uniqlo collection built around the humble winter fleece, with soft pink and small floral details. She likes layering a big fleece over a full, dressy piece to mix a sporty look with something sweeter. She also suggests balancing soft pastels with darker blacks and blues instead of dressing in one tone.
items.tip: Layer a cozy fleece or oversized knit over a dress or skirt for a mix of sporty and pretty.

items.title: The Street Style Guide to Dressing for Thanksgiving
items.snippet: In these three influencer-approved trends, you’ll look as delicious as the Thanksgiving feast.
items.headline: Thanksgiving Dressing, Borrowed From Street Style
items.summary: Vogue suggests easy ideas for holiday dinners drawn from fashion month, including midi skirts, cozy cardigans, corduroys and plaid tweed jackets. The point is that you probably own at least a few of these pieces already. Comfort and a polished look can go together at the table.
items.tip: Pull out a cardigan and a midi skirt or corduroys and try them together before shopping for a gathering.

items.title: 5 Sneaker Trends We’re Seeing (and Wearing) Everywhere in 2027
items.headline: Five Sneaker Trends Worth Trying Next
items.summary: Glamour rounds up the shapes it sees everywhere, from very slim soles and retro runners to Mary Jane sneakers, soft plimsolls and technical hiking-style trainers. Many of them look dressier or more feminine than classic sneakers, so they can work for the office as well as weekends. Socks play a big role in how each pair looks.
items.tip: Wear your sneakers with a different style of sock, such as crew, sheer or colorful, to see how it changes the outfit.

practice: Start by shopping your closet. Pull out your best coat, any midi skirt, a cardigan, grey or neutral trousers and the boots and trainers you wear most. Try three outfits: skirt with boots under your coat, trousers with chunky trainers and a scarf, and a cardigan layered over a dress. Notice which coat fits comfortably over knitwear and which shoes leave awkward gaps.

If you do buy something, pick one piece that fills a gap: a wool-blend coat in camel, navy or grey, or a pair of suede-look boots in brown. Look in budget and mid-range shops, and check seams, fabric and fit before you pay. Then let that piece work with what you have, such as a neutral coat over trousers, a cardigan and trainers, or a midi skirt with boots, so every outfit feels pulled together without a big spend.
